note: What Squamish Wants: specific asks residents answer yes, no or don't mind. These are the starter asks, each from the public record with a source. Residents add more on the site (stored in the database by api/wants.js). status: none | plan | agenda | done | province. who: council | province. area: a neighbourhood slug from data/neighbourhoods.json, or null for the whole town.

asks.title: Clear the encampment behind Under One Roof
asks.why: An encampment has grown behind Squamish's only shelter building on Third Avenue. Council and BC Housing are deciding what happens next.
asks.other_side: People camped there have nowhere else to go until temporary housing opens.
asks.source_label: Issues we follow: Under One Roof

asks.title: Let people stay at Under One Roof until temporary housing opens
asks.why: The same decision as clearing the encampment, asked the other way round.
asks.other_side: Neighbours and businesses say the camp has gone on too long and the area needs to be cleared now.
asks.source_label: Issues we follow: Under One Roof

asks.title: Put the modular shelter somewhere other than the park near Junction Park
asks.why: More than 290 residents signed a petition in April 2026 asking for a different site for the provincial modular housing. They don't oppose the program itself.
asks.other_side: Any site will have neighbours, and moving it can delay housing for people who need it now.

asks.title: Build the supportive housing at 39900 Government Road as planned
asks.why: BC Housing plans six storeys with 65 studio homes and support staff around the clock, run by Squamish Helping Hands.
asks.other_side: Some neighbours worry about the location and want more say in how it is run.
asks.source_label: Issues we follow: Government Road housing

asks.title: Install the defibrillator at the Brennan Park pickleball and tennis courts this year
asks.why: Pickleball Squamish offered up to $4,000 toward it. A June 2026 staff report scheduled it for 2027.
asks.other_side: The cabinet and data plan add yearly costs, and staff time is already planned for other work this year.

asks.title: Build more pickleball courts now instead of waiting for the 2027 parks plan
asks.why: In March 2026 staff asked council to hold off on new courts until the 2027 Parks and Recreation Master Plan looks at racket sports.
asks.other_side: Waiting for the plan means courts go where they are needed most, alongside tennis and other sports.

asks.title: Fix up the Eaglewind courts and reopen them for tennis
asks.why: The courts have sat unused since pickleball moved to Brennan Park in 2023 and 2024. Staff recommended fixing them up.
asks.other_side: The money could go toward courts in a busier spot.

asks.title: Build a second sheet of ice at Brennan Park
asks.why: Brennan Park has the town's only arena. A second rink is part of the District's long term vision, with no money set aside yet.
asks.other_side: A second rink costs tens of millions to build and run, which means borrowing or higher taxes.

asks.title: Build a second pool at Brennan Park
asks.why: Brennan Park has the town's only public pool. A second pool is part of the District's long term vision, with no money set aside yet.
asks.other_side: A second pool costs tens of millions to build and run, which means borrowing or higher taxes.

asks.title: Fence the off leash dog area at John Hunter Park
asks.why: John Hunter Park is one of the off leash pilot sites. The District says it still needs a fence, with no timeline set.
asks.other_side: Some park users would rather keep the park open and unfenced for everyone.
asks.source_label: District of Squamish: off leash pilot

asks.title: Upgrade the Brennan Park disc golf course
asks.why: Residents asked for an upgraded disc golf course in the 2021 feedback on the Brennan Park plan.
asks.other_side: Park money is tight and other Brennan Park projects are further along.

asks.title: Build covered outdoor basketball courts
asks.why: Residents asked for covered outdoor courts in the 2021 feedback on the Brennan Park plan, so they can be used in the rain.
asks.other_side: A roof adds a lot to the cost of a court.

asks.title: Add a crosswalk and a wider bike lane on Highlands Way North, south of Pentland Way
asks.why: Speeding in the school zone. It is on the District's 2026 traffic calming list.
asks.other_side: Some drivers say the changes slow a main route out of the Highlands.

asks.title: Put speed humps on Upper Mamquam Road
asks.why: Speeding and truck traffic. It is on the District's 2026 traffic calming list.
asks.other_side: Speed humps slow emergency vehicles and are hard on trucks that need the road.

asks.title: Put a raised crosswalk and new signs on Skyline Drive
asks.why: It is on the District's 2026 traffic calming list.
asks.other_side: Raised crosswalks slow everyone, including buses and emergency vehicles.

asks.title: Make the Highway 99 and Cleveland Avenue intersection safer
asks.why: The District says it has the highest crash rate in town. The Province runs the highway, so council's role is to press for changes.
asks.other_side: The Province added a lane there in 2022 and may not fund more work soon.
asks.source_label: District of Squamish: Highway 99 at Cleveland

asks.title: Keep downtown parking free
asks.why: A 2023 study suggested paid parking downtown. Council chose to test it at Darrell Bay only.
asks.other_side: Paid parking frees up spots for shoppers and raises money without raising taxes.

asks.title: Get a public bus running to Vancouver and Whistler
asks.why: Squamish has local buses but no public bus to Vancouver or Whistler. It has been studied since 2015 and has stalled over who runs and pays for it.
asks.other_side: Squamish would likely have to pay part of the yearly cost through property taxes.

asks.title: Keep the 2027 property tax increase to the rate of inflation
asks.why: Property taxes rose 12.8% in 2026. Council is working on the 2027 budget now.
asks.other_side: Holding taxes down means cutting or delaying services, repairs and projects.

asks.title: Speed up dike upgrades, even if it means borrowing more
asks.why: Much of Squamish sits on a floodplain. The District raises dikes a section at a time, mostly when grants come through.
asks.other_side: Borrowing adds interest costs to future tax bills, and waiting for grants is cheaper.
